title: Jeroboam Son of Nebat
lead: The first king of the northern kingdom of Israel (about 931–910 BC), a former labor foreman of Solomon chosen by the prophet Ahijah, who set up gold calves at Bethel and Dan. 'The sin of Jeroboam' became the refrain by which Kings judges every northern king.

sections.b:
Jeroboam rises as Solomon's foreman over the labor of the house of Joseph, is promised ten tribes by Ahijah, and flees to Shishak of Egypt (1 Kings 11:26–40). After Rehoboam's harsh answer, the northern tribes make him king (1 Kings 12:20). Afraid that pilgrimage to Jerusalem will win his people back to David's house, he makes two gold calves, sets them at Bethel and Dan, appoints non-Levite priests and moves the autumn feast (1 Kings 12:25–33). A man of God from Judah condemns his altar (1 Kings 13), and Ahijah announces the end of his dynasty (1 Kings 14:1–18), which falls to Baasha (1 Kings 15:29).

Kings judges each later northern king by whether he "walked in the sins of Jeroboam," and blames Israel's fall to Assyria on them (2 Kings 17:21–23). Chronicles gives Abijah of Judah a speech against him (2 Chronicles 13:4–12). The Mishnah counts him among those who have no share in the world to come (Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:2).
